title: Agent-Based Model: Simulating a Virus Expansion Based on the Acceptance of Containment Measures
reasoning: The paper extensively models and simulates human behavior and decision-making regarding public health measures. It incorporates factors like 'individual responsibility,' 'citizen solidarity,' 'interpersonal trust,' and 'psychological needs' (hedonism, belongingness) through the HUMAT decision-making model. This core component evaluates the 'acceptability of preventive measures' and how these human factors, which involve moral and ethical considerations in a societal context, influence the spread of a virus. This goes beyond a superficial mention and forms a fundamental part of the model's design and analysis.
